payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_regate.py::test_review_commit_diff_keeps_the_review_commits_paths_the_task_also_changed stayed green with the criterion's own edit applied to saffron/regate.py. The claim was "`review_commit_diff(mirror, pushed_sha, baseline_sha, head)` in `saffron/regate.py` returns the diff `head`'s review commits make. When `pushed_sha` is an ancestor of `head` and is not `head`, the range starts at `pushed_sha`. The paths kept are those that `pushed_sha..head` and `baseline_sha..head` both change, each read with `DIFF_FLAGS`, so a rename counts as both of its paths. The result is `git diff` over that range with `DIFF_FLAGS`, limited to those paths in sorted order. A head whose only commit past `pushed_sha` merges the base branch returns empty. The witness builds a checkout that stands for the mirror, with `main` as the base branch. Its packaged commit edits src/p.py, src/q.py and tests/test_w.py. `main` then edits main.txt. A review commit edits tests/test_w.py again, sets src/q.py back to its base text, and renames tests/test_old.py to tests/test_new.py. A merge of `main` follows, as GitHub's update branch makes. `baseline_sha` is `main`'s head. The witness asserts the returned diff's paths are exactly tests/test_new.py, tests/test_old.py and tests/test_w.py. It asserts the text equals the test's own `DIFF_FLAGS` diff of `pushed_sha..head` over those three paths. A second head merges `main` straight onto the packaged commit, and returns empty.", and the whole `tests` gate stayed green under the edit too.
